standards.mechanism: Theme variables as CSS custom properties in the theme file (--amount-col, --action-col, no @theme mapping)
lucide-react pinned exactly with npm install --save-exact
Lucide React icon components, aria-hidden by default, currentColor, stroke-width 2
One custom icon (SearchPriority) with createLucideIcon(name, iconNode), typed as LucideIcon
Decorative images hidden from assistive technology; text carries the meaning and the accessible names are unchanged
Inline flex with baseline alignment for the wordmark dot; 44px target token on the home and top-nav links
Target size through the existing --tap-target token

Skip link first in tab order, hidden until focus, then absolutely positioned (out of the flow, so no layout shift and a click made while it is focused lands); no offsets, so it takes the static position of an absolute child of the header flex container (CSS Flexbox 4.1) and aligns with the home link; min-h-(--tap-target) like the home link, no raw px

The hint row uses a flex paragraph (gap-1.5, icon mt-0.5 shrink-0) so a wrapped hint keeps the icon on its first line; the mockup's docs/ux/mockups/app.css (.hint: gap 6px, .icon 14px with margin-top 1px, in the DisputeDesk-ux-docs checkout) gives the 6px gap and 1px offset, and mt-0.5 (2px) is the nearest theme-scale utility. QA to check against the mockup.
npm run build prints Vite's existing chunk-size warning; not compared with main.

Fix round 1 (review medium, routing.test.tsx): the top-navigation check is now getByRole(navigation, Main).querySelector(svg) toBeNull(), because an svg has no implicit role in @testing-library/dom 10.4.2 and the old queryByRole(img) could never fail. Break 9 puts a Lucide List icon in a TopNav link; verified: the test passes without it and fails with it.
QA's two e2e edits (e2e/tests/spa-disputes-history.spec.ts, e2e/tests/spa-transactions.spec.ts) are in the working tree unchanged; e2e/ was not edited in this round.

Fix round 3 (QA F4, medium): the skip link moved from RootLayout into Header, as the first child of the header's inner flex container, and Header takes a new onSkipToMain prop (RootLayout passes () => mainRef.current?.focus()). Reason: with no offsets, an absolutely positioned child of a flex container sits at the container's padding edge and centred on the cross axis (CSS Flexbox 4.1), exactly where the home link is, on every page width of the container (start page 1120px, other pages 1072px) and whatever the header's height, with no left/top utilities that could drift from the header's px-4 md:px-6 or min-h-16. It cost one deviation from the earlier test: 'before the header' became 'before the home link', because the skip link is now inside the banner landmark; it is still the first focusable element of the page (the first-Tab tests, the StrictMode tests and e2e spa-transactions 'visited' order are unchanged).

The skip link is at least as tall as the home link only while both use min-h-(--tap-target) and the home link is one line; the unit test pins both classes and the shared parent. It is 52.6px wider than the home link (the text 'Skip to main content' plus px-4 against the wordmark).

The unit test checks classes and the shared parent (jsdom has no layout), and that the skip link has no offset, inset or margin utility; the real geometry, hit test, no-shift check, pointer click and axe were confirmed in headless Chromium (smoke).

The unlinked screen has no link other than the skip link and home link, so the pointer check there presses the Sign out button and sees the logout request; the linked and anonymous states press links.

Each break's test_method is a shell command (cd frontend && npm ci --silent && npx vitest run <file> -t "<name>"), because the throwaway copy has no node_modules.
